art.title: Siberian Dogs in the Snow
art.why: No NGA prisoner or Siberian camp scene; this is a snow field named for Siberia (two white dogs in snow, per the description). Use as the winter of exile, not as a picture of prison.
No NGA painting of a lonely man in a room: candidates (Vrel, de Hooch) show women in Dutch interiors. Teach without a painting.

art.title: Street in Venice
art.why: A narrow, shadowed alley with a woman walking past two men in black: the dim city street the spec asks for (not St Petersburg; say so).

art.title: The Raising of Lazarus
art.why: REUSE of an existing art id: the NGA has no other Raising of Lazarus (searched titles and descriptions). It is exactly the scene Sonia reads; the spec asked for another, so the lead must agree to the reuse.

art.title: Christ Gathering His Garments after the Flagellation
art.why: No NGA Christ before Pilate or Inquisitor scene. Correa shows Christ alone and silent after his accusers have scourged him, the whip on the floor, angels lamenting: the silent Christ of Ivan's poem, made in Spain's empire (Mexico) in the age of the Inquisition (check Correa's Mexican origin from NGA record).

art.title: Saint Anthony Abbot and Saint Bernardino of Siena
art.why: Anthony, the first monk and father of the desert elders, white-bearded, reading, with staff: the line of elders Zosima stands in. Western, not Orthodox: say so.

art.title: Green Wheat Fields, Auvers
art.why: The grain of wheat of John 12:24, the novel's epigraph: green fields rolling under a swirling sky.

music.why: The Russian Orthodox all-night vigil: the worship Dostoevsky returned to after Siberia.

The music of Orthodox monastic prayer, the world of Optina and Zosima.

memory.title: Unless a grain of wheat
memory.ref: John 12:24 (WEB): "Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit."

memory.title: Love all God's creation
memory.ref: The Brothers Karamazov, Book VI ch. 3(g) 'Of Prayer, of Love, and of Contact with other Worlds' (Garnett 1912): the passage beginning 'Love all God's creation, the whole and every grain of sand in it.' Extract verbatim from Gutenberg #28054.
